quarterly_data.signal: MARA 10-Q: Q2 2026 bitcoin mining revenue was $170,066 thousand versus $228,779 thousand a year earlier; other digital assets mining revenue was $237 thousand versus $3,598 thousand, and hosting services revenue was nil versus $1,164 thousand. Average BTC per day was 26.6 versus 25.9, the average price of BTC mined $71,325 versus $98,975, blocks won 700 versus 694, and transaction fees 0.7% of the total versus 1.4%. First-half bitcoin mining revenue was $342,228 thousand versus $436,538 thousand, with 4,669 BTC produced versus 4,644.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 bitcoin mining revenue $170,066 thousand; H1 $342,228 thousand; 700 blocks won

quarterly_data.signal: MARA 10-Q revenue disaggregation for arrangements in which MARA is the Operator and Participant (mining): Q2 2026 mining operator block rewards were $156,492 thousand versus $218,309 thousand a year earlier, mining operator transaction fees $1,044 thousand versus $3,044 thousand, and mining participant revenue $12,767 thousand versus $11,024 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 operator block rewards $156,492 thousand; participant $12,767 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: MARA 10-Q fleet: miner efficiency was 17.3 joules per terahash at June 30, 2026 versus 18.3 a year earlier, with energized hashrate of 70.3 EH/s versus 57.4 EH/s. Q2 2026 third-party hosting and other energy costs were $69,156 thousand versus $69,029 thousand, and purchased energy costs $48,750 thousand versus $41,730 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: 17.3 J/TH; 57.4 EH/s a year earlier; Q2 hosting and other energy costs $69,156 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: MARA 10-Q contractual obligations as of June 30, 2026: purchase agreements for miners and other mining equipment of $64,552 thousand, all short-term; other purchase obligations of $314,126 thousand ($127,724 thousand short-term, $186,402 thousand long-term), consisting of contracts for hosting MARA's equipment and operational support in data centers where its equipment is deployed.
